title: Postmortem Automation and Causal Mapping Standard
author: Aisha Gupta
body:
Summary:
This standard defines how Redwood SRE teams automate post-incident workflows and apply structured causal mapping to incident reviews. It prescribes templates, telemetry requirements, evidence collection automation, and the minimal artifact set required before an incident is considered reviewable. The goal is faster, higher-quality retrospectives and improved SLO-driven remediation velocity.

Why this doc exists:
- Reduce time between incident closure and blameless analysis by automating evidence collection and initial causal triage.
- Ensure consistent mapping from symptoms → root causes → corrective actions with ownership and measurable follow-ups.
- Tie incident severity and remediations back to service-level objectives and error budgets.

Scope:
- Applies to all production incidents impacting Redwood-hosted inference, Dedicated pools, and Private deployments when SLOs are breached or an outage >= P2 occurs.
- Excludes: low-impact operational tasks (P3/P4) where a lightweight postmortem is adequate.

Definitions (quick):
- SLO: service-level objective monitored by the SRE SLO exporter.
- Error budget: remaining allowed failure % used for release gating and capacity decisions.
- Causal map: directed, time-ordered graph describing symptom, contributing factors, root cause, and mitigations.
- Postmortem Automation: scriptable evidence collection, bucketization, and draft generation for reviewer triage.

Governance and ownership:
- Incident Commander (IC): responsible for declaring incident severity and triggering the automation pipeline.
- Evidence Automation Owner: team that maintains the postmortem automation scripts (owned by eng-sre/operational-tooling).
- Reviewer lead: senior SRE assigned within 5 business days to shepherd the review to publication.
- Action owners: explicitly assigned engineers with deadlines for corrective actions.

Mandatory telemetry and evidence for automated collection (minimal artifact set):
1) SLO telemetry snapshot (last 72 hours): 99th/95th/50th latency, availability, and per-tenant error rates.
2) Alert timeline: full alert stream with rule IDs and firing windows.
3) Autoscale/capacity events: node/GPU pool changes, preemption events, pod restarts, and scheduler throttles.
4) Request traces and sampled logs (span IDs mapped to requests) for up to 1,000 representative requests.
5) Configuration diff: model version, routing policy, quantization profile, and canary status at incident start vs baseline.
6) Deployment manifests and rollout statuses (canary percentage, rollback events).

Causal mapping methodology (how to construct the map):
- Step 0: Seed the map automatically from telemetry: alerts, trace counts, and top stacktraces. The automation creates an initial incident graph.
- Step 1: Label nodes as Symptom / Contributing Factor / Candidate Root Cause / Human Process Failure / Known Bug.
- Step 2: Establish temporal edges (A -> B) with timestamps; prefer "immediately precedes" semantics where determinable.
- Step 3: Identify the smallest set of change events that, when reverted or mitigated, remove the symptom (counterfactual test).
- Step 4: Classify detection and mitigation gaps: instrumentation gap, alert threshold tuning, autoscale misconfiguration, regression in model bundle, etc.
- Step 5: Attach quantitative evidence to each edge (error spikes, increased latency %s, CPU/GPU utilization delta).

Automated postmortem pipeline (end-to-end):
1) Trigger: IC marks incident closed in incident-dispatcher (or via /api/incidents/{id}/close).
2) Evidence collection: postmortem-agent runs collectors (slo-exporter, trace-harvester, deployment-census).
3) Draft generation: template engine produces a Markdown draft with sections pre-populated and a preliminary causal map image (SVG).
4) Pre-review triage: automation routes draft to reviewer lead and notifies related owners via Slack and email.
5) Human enrichment: reviewers augment causal map, validate edges, add corrective action items and mitigations.
6) Publication: review publishes final postmortem to Confluence and links to the incident ticket.

Template requirements for the draft (automated fields):
- Title: <service> incident: <short descriptor> (ID:INC-####)
- Timebox: Start, mitigation complete, full recovery, business impact window.
- SLO impact summary: measured breach, error budget consumed, % of customers affected.
- Evidence links: direct presigned URLs to telemetry bundles.
- Initial causal map SVG (auto-generated).
- Proposed corrective actions (auto-suggested from previous incidents by similarity scoring).

Runbook checklist for publishable postmortem (must be met before publication):
1) Automation has attached the SLO snapshot and alert timeline.
2) At least one reviewer assigned and first review comment added.
3) Action items enumerated, with owners and due dates in the doc.
4) Mitigation verification steps: either automated regression test or rollout guard added.
5) If incident consumed >25% of monthly error budget for any SLO, schedule a QBR slot for the affected product.

Severity-specific guidance and pathways:
- P0/P1 (SLO outage > severe): require full causal map + triage workshop within 3 business days; all action items <=30 days unless escalated.
- P2 (partial degradation): require causal map and automation-sourced evidence; action items <=60 days.
- P3/P4: lightweight retrospective; optional automation artifacts.

Operational tooling integrations (must support these features):
- SLO Exporter: export SLI windows and histograms to postmortem-agent.
- Trace Harvester: sample trace reconstruction (linkable by request id).
- Incident Dispatcher: create/close incidents and trigger automation.
- Runbook Dispatcher: attach runbook excerpts to causal map nodes.
- Evidence Archive: short-term presigned storage for 90 days, encrypted.
- Similarity Engine: suggests prior incidents with analogous causal graphs.

Examples: evidence snippet and generated causal map legend (text representation):
- Symptom: "API-GEN-01: 500 errors spiked from 0.1% to 8% at 2026-02-18T14:12Z"
- Contributing factor: "Autoscaler delayed scale by 3m due to stale metric collector"
- Candidate root cause: "Prometheus exporter regression dropped per-pod req_count metric"
- Mitigation: "Re-apply exporter hotfix v1.2.3 and restart exporter; add alert for metric drop"

Sample automated evidence collection command (for operators):
- curl -X POST https://incident-dispatcher.internal/api/incidents/INC-1234/collect -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'

Causal mapping table (text):
| Node ID | Type | Timestamp | Evidence link | Proposed action | Owner | Due |
| N1 | Symptom | 2026-02-18T14:12Z | link-to-slo-snapshot | Rollback model addon | @eng-ml | 2026-03-01 |
| N2 | Contributing | 2026-02-18T14:09Z | link-to-autoscale | Fix metric exporter | @infra | 2026-02-25 |

Post-incident automation safety checks (pre-publish):
- Ensure PII is scrubbed from logs in the archived bundle.
- Validate links are accessible to the reviewer group.
- If automation fails to collect trace examples, escalate to Evidence Automation Owner.

Actioning and follow-through:
- All action items must include acceptance criteria (how we know the fix works), test plans, and monitoring queries to validate.
- Quarterly SLO review includes a roll-up of automated postmortem metrics: mean time to publish, average number of contributing factors per incident, fraction of incidents with automated causal maps.

Change control and rollout for this standard:
1) Pilot: apply to P0/P1 incidents for 3 months; gather metrics and feedback.
2) Iterate: update template and automation scripts with lessons from pilot.
3) Adopt: require for P0/P1 and recommended for P2 after adoption milestone.

Appendix A — Quick checklist for an IC when closing an incident:
1) Mark incident as closed in incident-dispatcher.
2) Confirm automated evidence collection run succeeded (exit code 0).
3) Confirm SLO exporter snapshot attached.
4) Assign reviewer lead and set 10 business day review deadline.

Appendix B — Failure modes the automation should surface (examples):
- Missing metric exporters, uneven sampling in traces, presigned link expiry during review, inability to reconstruct request IDs across services.
